title: Tactical targeted model pinning and rollback orchestration for cross-environment canary regressions
creator: Miguel Torres
description:
Summary: During a progressive rollout of model-v2026-03B we observed correlated failures across Hosted canaries and two Dedicated pools: increased token-level error rate (misformatted structured outputs), 20–40% latency spike p50->p90 for short requests, and a regression in answer fidelity for three paying customers (Acme Health, FileWave, NimbusRetail). Private customers reported a mismatch in behavior for quantized variants after local compilation. Multiple PagerDuty pages opened and at least two customer SEs escalated to support.

Goal: Implement a reliable, low-blast-radius mitigation path that (1) addresses urgent customer issues, (2) prevents noisy global rollback when unnecessary, and (3) provides coordinated post-incident follow-up (root cause and preventative work).

Scope: Hosted API routes, Dedicated GPU pools, and Private on-prem model catalog pinning. The plan covers immediate mitigation, verification, communication, and next steps for permanent fixes.
decisions: Adopt targeted route-level pinning to previous stable model variant (v2026-02Z) for affected customers instead of full-cluster rollback to minimize blast radius.
Use routing policy override + traffic steering for Dedicated pools to move only affected tenant pools to fallback model while preserving autoscale for others.
Schedule hotfix branch for runtime kernel selection bug; deploy as canaryed patch to control-plane nodes before wider rollout.
Do not perform immediate DB/metadata migration during rollback window to avoid additional risk; apply after stability confirmed.
Require E2E verification on a synthetic prompt set (see links) before marking incident resolved.
